title: Fractions you will actually use
hook: Which is bigger, a 3/8 inch drill bit or a 5/16, and how many three-quarter-metre tails come off a 6 m length of cable?
oneBreath: A fraction is one number. The bottom names the size of the piece and the top counts the pieces. Give two fractions the same size of piece and you can compare them, add them and take them away. To find a fraction of something, divide by the bottom and multiply by the top. Dividing by a fraction asks how many of it fit.

ideas.title: What a fraction is
ideas.oneLine: A fraction is one number. The bottom names the size of the equal pieces and the top counts them.

ideas.title: Equivalent fractions
ideas.oneLine: Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number and the fraction keeps its size.

ideas.title: Mixed numbers
ideas.oneLine: A fraction bigger than 1 can be written two ways, as a top-heavy fraction or as wholes and a fraction.

ideas.title: Comparing fractions
ideas.oneLine: To see which fraction is bigger, give both the same size of piece, then compare the tops.

ideas.title: Adding and taking away
ideas.oneLine: Fractions add or take away only when their pieces match, so match the bottoms first, then work with the tops.

ideas.title: A fraction of an amount
ideas.oneLine: To find a fraction of an amount, divide by the bottom number, then multiply by the top.

ideas.title: Multiplying fractions
ideas.oneLine: To multiply fractions, multiply the tops together and the bottoms together.

ideas.title: Dividing fractions
ideas.oneLine: Dividing by a fraction asks how many of it fit, which is why you flip it and multiply.

calibration.why: In fifteenths, 2/3 is 10/15 and 3/5 is 9/15, so 2/3 is bigger.
In sixths, 1/2 is 3/6 and 1/3 is 2/6, so together they make 5/6.
